file_impact.reason: new section 2c: publish mem_available_percent / mem_used_percent / mem_probe_ok as dimensionless host gauges from `free -k` column 7 (available, not free), plus container_memory_rss_bytes per container and container_stats_ok, with docker stats bounded by --no-stream and timeout so it cannot wedge the 5-minute timer

NEW: emit a GATE_PEAK_RSS journald marker at gate completion carrying peak_rss_bytes and peak_delta_bytes; ru_maxrss_to_bytes is a pure function because the unit differs by platform (bytes on darwin, KiB on Linux). A marker rather than metric plumbing because the containers deliberately hold no AWS credentials
wrap the review_plan library entry point, the seam both the MCP daemon-thread path and the CLI reach the gate through
same wrap for verify_completion; emitted from a finally so a run that DIES (the OOM case this exists for) still reports
the oracle for the shell probe: publishes on failure paths rather than nothing, reads `available` not `free`, and docker stats is bounded (proven by hanging the stub for 300s)
the oracle for the marker: emitted from finally, correct unit handling per platform, and the f829 rule that the logger copy omits the token
